dedupe_keys.name: the net sustainability impact of shared micromobility in six global cities fraunhofer isi 2022

description: This report by Konstantin Krauss and Claus Doll of the Fraunhofer Institute for Systems and Innovation Research ISI with Calvin Thigpen of Lime, dated 25 October 2022 and undertaken as a commission from Lime, gives a 2022 update of the net emissions impact of shared e-scooters and e-bikes. Coverage: survey data from 4,167 shared micromobility riders in Berlin, Dusseldorf, Paris, Stockholm, Melbourne and Seattle; existing life cycle assessment data adapted to each city's characteristics, and information from a shared micromobility provider. The largest shifts are from walking, public transport, ride-hailing and private vehicles; in all six cities shared micromobility reduces emissions compared with the modes replaced, more for e-scooters than e-bikes because of embedded carbon and life spans. Format and access: a 43-page PDF. Licence and cost: free to read; no licence stated. Caveats: funded by and co-authored with the operator, as the authors declare. The mode shift shares and per-city emission factors can set micromobility substitution in urban transport climate mitigation models. It relates to the life cycle study of shared e-scooters in 100 EU cities and the BTS bikeshare and e-scooter systems data in the catalogue.
